thesis: A ceiling is not a cable. Every Alaskan connection to the wider world, a chatbot question included, leaves on four aging undersea cables that land in Oregon and Washington, and AIDEA's new Northstar Fiber Development is a well-guarded option to add a door, whose test is whether bound customers sign before December 31st, 2028.
supporting_facts: c5/c6/c7/c8 four subsea cables plus one land route, three land in Oregon and one in Washington, two from 1999 against a typical 25 year design life per AIDEA
c9/c10/c12 AIDEA's own digital cul-de-sac line, no cable direct to Asia, Asia third and only explore and collaborate
c14/c15/c16 no project, partner or route, binding customer commitments required, authority ends December 31st, 2028
counterpoint_honored: Conditions, a ceiling and a landing rule are how careful public money should look, and the need is documented (c3, c13, c8). The film grants all of it, then narrows the claim: the economics AIDEA cites are Nordic and European (c18), and neither document says AI (c17), so the AI link is Alaska.Ai's own framing.
falsifiable: False if the authority reaches December 31st, 2028 with no finance plan and no binding customer commitment ever being needed, or if any Alaska cable reached Asia directly or the four landed anywhere but the Pacific Northwest.
runner_ups: Enthusiast: a door built before choosing where it leads (loses: cheerleading with no route)
Dramatist: a permission slip, not a cable (loses: right facts, sour frame)
cross_challenge: Three analysts each red-teamed their own thesis against c14, c15 and c18, and the synthesis adopts the stricter falsifier. No separate cross-challenge round ran.
